thread:
taylor: quick flag — after landing the "favor_micro_kernels" tweak we saw ingress host CPU p95 for tokenize+parse up ~27% in the canary window.

nina: ouch. flame or counters? is the extra CPU actually in tokenization or in syscalls from streaming?

taylor: quick flame excerpt from a 90s sample: 
```
CPU 90s
  ingress/tokenize.go:emitTokens    23s (25%)
  ingest/parse.go:parseFrames       11s (12%)
  grpc/emit.go:writevFlush           8s (9%)
  kvcache/client.go:lookupBatch     5s (6%)
  selector/score.go:scoreCandidates  3s (3%)
```

raj: selector scoring light but did it shift distribution massively? micro kernels + same framing probably increases small-frame frequency.

taylor: selector counts: micro variant went from 4%->44% in canary. tcp write-size p95 dropped from 580B->220B; small-write rate (<300B) went 20%->64%. kv hit-rate dipped ~3.2%.

chao: that explains syscall pressure and parse churn. are we appending variant tags to kvcache keys? extra bytes could matter.

taylor: yes we add "-micro" suffix for the variant in cache keys. average key len +7 bytes.

nina: immediate mitigation options: revert favor_micro_kernels in canary; increase minibatch timeout to allow more coalescing; or add a host-side coalesce guard in grpc writer (buffer until >=512B or timeout).

deploy-bot: deploy-canary chao/revert-micro-bias -> ingress-canary-a started at 2850007805 :rocket:

taylor: spun revert in canary. collecting p95/p99 and socket histograms now.

raj: also add lightweight metrics: parse_bytes_per_request and grpc_coalesce_misses/sec. we need to quantify the host framing penalty.

chao: prototype plan: implement soft coalesce with config "grpc_soft_coalesce_bytes=512" and a fallback to current behavior. run A/B with streaming traces.

nina: plus unit test that simulates fragmentation: forced stream boundaries and forced micro-variant choice so we can reproduce locally.

taylor: after 14m post-revert: parse CPU down ~21%, small writes down ~57%, kv hit-rate returned to baseline. p99 tail unchanged.

raj: good signal. long-term we should bake an expected-host-writes estimate into the selector cost function so kernel choices that blow up host IO are penalized. I'll sketch INF-5120.

chao: I'll land the coalesce guard as a fast patch (config default 512) and add the new metrics. also will export selector variant counts to the perf dashboard so we can see distribution by trace type.

nina: also add a perf-harness scenario: streaming-heavy corpus + selector changes. kernel-only microbenchmarks miss these cross-layer effects.

taylor: agreed. I'll open the PRs: revert + coalesce + tests. and draft the RFC to include host-framing penalty in selector scoring.

deploy-bot: canary completed at 2850008100 \u2705 3/3 healthy.

nina: excellent. adding a short postmortem note: "selector <-> host framing interaction" to catch future regressions.

raj: INF-5120 opened and assigned to runtime/selector. chao will own the coalesce writer PR.

chao: PR created, linking perf results once A/B run finishes. thanks for the quick rollback/triage.

taylor: thanks all — learned a lot about cross-layer costs. checklist item: any kernel selection change requires streaming-fragmentation perf runs.
